title: PRA approvals: requesting, reviewing and expiry

prose.text: Approvals bound when a user can reach a console. A user requests a window, an admin approves it, and access ends when the window does.

prose.label: Creating one.
prose.text: {{access-policy-required}} {{user-email-nameid}} The page's statement that there is no limit on segments conflicts with the documented figure {{divergence:segments-per-approval}}. {{time-window}} Which time zone applies by default is open {{gap:working-hours-default}}.

prose.label: Users that do not exist yet.
prose.text: {{user-validation}} {{emergency-user-window}} When the window appears is described two ways {{divergence:emergency-window-domains}}.

prose.label: Reviewing.
prose.text: {{approver-view}} {{request-metadata}} {{portal-review}} Whether more than one approver can be required is open {{gap:multi-approver}}.

Which consoles require an approval is open {{gap:approval-optional}}. The SDK and Ansible handling of approvals, including working hours, is in [[zpa.pra.tooling]]. The portals policy that enables requesting and reviewing is in [[zpa.pra.portals-policy]], the Emergency Access side of creating users is in [[zpa.emergency-access.configuration]], and the approvals limit is in [[zpa.pra.components:limits]].

The Terraform PRA approval doc limits an approval to one email address, a start no more than an hour in the past and an end within 365 days [[zpa.terraform.resource-constraints:pra-approval-single-email-window]].

checks.do: Whether the user's window has started or ended, since an expired approval removes access and an upcoming one shows as Future.
Whether an approval is Active, Future or Expired and so editable, and whether an access policy with the privileged approval option exists, since without it the approval does not take effect.
Whether a segment count answer rests on the limit or on the page that says there is none.
Whether the user can see My Requests and My Reviews, which need the admin enablement, the My Approvals feature and a portals policy.
Whether the Add Emergency Access User window should have appeared, given the two descriptions of when it does.
Whether the request exists in the Approval Requests table and with which status.
Whether the per-user request count or the tenant approval count is at its limit.
Whether an answer assumes multi-approver support or per-console approval requirements, which no source states.

request-flow.statement: Once an admin has enabled privileged requests in a portals policy, a user creates an approval request on the My Requests page of the PRA Portal by choosing a microtenant (Default is preselected) and consoles, a start date and a duration, and optionally a reason, then saving it for review.

quotes: After the admin has enabled privileged requests in a portals policy, you can access the My Requests page in the PRA Portal.
Click the My Requests tab.
Select a Microtenant from the drop-down menu. The Default Microtenant is automatically selected.
Select privileged consoles.
Select a start date in the calendar.
Select the duration that you want this privileged approval to last.
(Optional) Enter a reason for access.
The saved privileged approval request appears on the My Requests page and is ready to be reviewed by an approver.

approver-view.statement: Requests are reviewed on the Approval Requests page, which can be filtered by console and requester, where each one can be approved or rejected. The table shows requested duration and approved duration separately.

quotes: To view privileged approval request data, go to Zero Trust Browser > Privileged Remote Access > Approval Requests.
Console: See logs for a specific privileged console.
Requester: See logs for a specific user who requested a privileged approval.
Requested Duration: The length of time that the access for the privileged approval is requested for.
Approved Duration: The length of time that the access for the privileged approval is available for.
You can approve or reject the privileged approval requests by clicking the following:

request-metadata.statement: Each request records the requester, policy name, approval ID, start and end time, duration, console, requested and approved duration, reason, status (Approved or Rejected) and the time it was requested.

quotes: Policy Name: The name of the access policy associated with the privileged approval request.
Approval ID: Click the displayed ID to view the approval in a window.
Start Time: The set start time that the user has access to the Privileged Remote Access (PRA) Portal.
End Time: The set end time that the user no longer has access to the PRA Portal.
Console: The privileged console that the privileged approval request was created for.
Requested Duration: The length of time that the access for the privileged approval is requested for.
Approved Duration: The length of time that the access for the privileged approval is available for.
Reason: If a reason was included during the creation of the privileged approval request, it is displayed here.
Requested Time: The time stamp of when the privileged approval request was created.
Status: The status of the privileged approval request (Approved or Rejected).
Duration: The length of time that the access for the privileged approval is available for.
evidence.after: End Time: The set end time that the user no longer has access to the PRA Portal.

window-expiry.statement: After the approved window ends the user loses access to the console. Approvals whose window has ended show as Expired, upcoming ones show as Future, and an admin can purge expired approvals to clean up the table.

quotes: If an end user has a privileged approval assigned to their privileged consoles, they lose access when the scheduled time expires.
Privileged consoles with privileged approvals that have ended due to the time window completing show as Expired.
Any scheduled privileged consoles with upcoming time windows of access show as Future.
Admins can clean up their privileged approvals table by purging expired privileged approvals.

request-limit.statement: Each user can create up to 20 privileged approval requests on the My Requests page, and only approvals in Future or Active status count toward the 20,000-approval limit.

quotes: Each user can create up to 20 privileged approval requests on the My Requests page
Only privileged approvals with approval statuses of Future or Active are counted.
20,000 privileged approvals

email-scoped.statement: Privileged approvals allow third-party users and contractors to log in to a PRA Portal, maintain a secure access point only for the email addresses included in a privileged approval, and give those users entry to the specific applications they need to access.

quotes: Privileged approvals allow third-party users and contractors to be able to log in to a Privileged Remote Access (PRA) Portal.
Privileged approvals maintain a secure access point only for the email addresses you include in a privileged approval.
These users are given entry to the specific applications you need them to access.

admin-actions.statement: An admin can create privileged approvals with a set amount of time that one or more designated application segments can be accessed, delete existing approvals to revoke access to those segments, and delete all expired approvals.

quotes: Create privileged approvals with a set amount of time that one or more designated application segments can be accessed.
Delete existing privileged approvals to revoke access to those application segments.
Delete all expired privileged approvals.

access-policy-required.statement: After a privileged portal and privileged console are created, privileged approvals can be created. A privileged approval needs an access policy that uses the Conditional Access rule action with the Allow for Privileged Approval checkbox selected to take effect, and an approval created before that access policy and its application segments cannot take effect until the policy is created. The access policy page names the same checkbox Allow with Privileged Approval, so the label differs between pages.

quotes: After you have created a privileged portal and privileged console, you can start creating privileged approvals to allow users into the PRA Portal.
You also need to create an access policy that uses the Conditional Access rule action with the Allow for Privileged Approval checkbox selected for a privileged approval to take effect.

If you create a privileged approval before setting an access policy, the privileged approval and its related application segments cannot take effect until the access policy is created with the related application segments.
The Allow with Privileged Approval checkbox is only an option if you have

access-policy-required.conditions: Only the label differs between the approvals pages (Allow for Privileged Approval) and the access policy page (Allow with Privileged Approval); which one the Admin Console shows is not stated. See zpa.pra.access-policy:allow-with-privileged-approval.

approvals-table.statement: The Privileged Approvals page lists each approval's User Email, Application Segments, Start Time and End Time, and an approval status of Active (currently available), Expired (no longer available) or Future (available at a set time in the future). Approvals with an Expired status cannot be edited, and only Active and Future approvals include the Edit icon.

quotes: User Email: The email address for the user assigned to the privileged approval.
Application Segments: The application segments selected for the privileged approval.
Start Time: The set start time that the user has access to the PRA Portal.
End Time: The set end time that the user no longer has access to the PRA Portal.
Active: The privileged approval is currently available for the user.
Expired: The privileged approval is no longer available for the user.
Future: The privileged approval is available for the user at a set time in the future.
Privileged approvals with an Expired approval status cannot be edited. Only privileged approvals with Active and Future approval statuses include the Edit icon.

microtenant-disabled.statement: If Privileged Approvals are disabled in a Microtenant, only users with the matching authentication domains are applicable, and a third-party user or contractor using such a Microtenant cannot add or edit a privileged approval.

quotes: If Privileged Approvals are disabled in the Microtenant, only users with the matching authentication domains are applicable.
If you are a third-party user or contractor using a Microtenant with Privileged Approvals disabled, you cannot edit an existing privileged approval.
If you are a third-party user or contractor using a Microtenant with Privileged Approvals disabled, you cannot add a privileged approval.

user-email-nameid.statement: The user email on a privileged approval should match the tenant's identity provider (IdP), specifically the NameID attribute in the SAML Assertion.

quotes: The user email should match the tenant's identity provider (IdP), specifically the NameID attribute in the SAML Assertion.

time-window.statement: An approval's time window has a start and end date, time and time zone; the end user cannot use the console before the scheduled time and loses access after it expires. For windows spanning multiple days, optional working hours set the hours and days of the week of access, with a default of 9:00 start time and 17:00 end time for a 24-hour window.

quotes: Choose a start and end date, time, and time zone that the end user is authorized to use the privileged console.
The end user cannot use the privileged console before the scheduled time, and after the time expires, the end user loses access to that privileged console.
For time windows spanning multiple days, you can configure working hours as well as the days of the week for which access is permitted.

(Optional) Select the Enable Working Hours checkbox to specify what hours and days of the week the time window is going to be active. The default is 9:00 start time and 17:00 end time for a 24-hour window.

time-window.conditions: The phrase for a 24-hour window is the page's own wording and is not interpreted here.

user-validation.statement: When Emergency Access is not configured, Private Access does not validate that users exist before a privileged approval is created, and those users are managed in the IdP. When Emergency Access is configured, Private Access validates only users from arbitrary authentication domains, and if the user does not exist in the IdP enabled for Emergency Access it offers to create the user when the approval is created, after which the user can be managed on the Emergency Access Users page.

quotes: When Emergency Access isn't configured, Private Access doesn't validate that users exist before a privileged approval is created. You need to manage those users within your IdP.
When Emergency Access is configured, Private Access only validates users that are from arbitrary authentication domains.

If the user does not exist in the IdP enabled for Emergency Access, Private Access offers to create the user when creating the privileged approval, and you can manage the user on the Emergency Access Users page.

emergency-user-window.statement: The Add Emergency Access User window appears only if the email address does not match the authentication domain of the primary or secondary domain, Emergency Access is already configured, the specified email domain is added to the Emergency Authentication Domains field, and the user does not exist in the IdP enabled for Emergency Access. After the admin fills in the email address, first name and last name and clicks OK, the user is added to the Emergency Access Users page.

quotes: The Add Emergency Access User window only appears if:
The email address entered doesn't match the authentication domain of the primary or secondary domain.
Emergency Access is already configured.
The specified email domain is added to the Emergency Authentication Domains field.
The user doesn't exist in the IdP enabled for Emergency Access.
Email Address: The email address of the privileged approval user.
First Name: The first name of the privileged approval user.
Last Name: The last name of the privileged approval user.
Click OK, and the user is added to the Emergency Access Users page.

my-approvals-prerequisites.statement: If an admin has enabled privileged requests and approvals for the PRA Portal and a user has the My Approvals feature enabled, the user can access and manage privileged requests and approvals on the My Requests and My Reviews pages. The admin must also configure a portals policy to enable requesting and reviewing approvals.

quotes: If an admin has enabled privileged requests and approvals for the Privileged Remote Access (PRA) Portal, and a user has the My Approvals feature enabled, then the user can access and manage privileged requests and approvals on the My Requests and My Reviews pages.
The admin must also configure a portals policy to enable requesting and reviewing approvals.

my-requests-and-reviews.statement: The My Requests page displays the privileged approval requests a user has created and the My Reviews page those the user has permission to approve and reject. My Requests lists Console, Microtenant, Start Date, Requested Duration, Approved Duration (access ends after it) and a status of Pending, Approved, Expired or Rejected, My Reviews adds the Requester, and request analytics are on the Requests page.

quotes: The My Requests page displays the privileged approval requests that a user has created.
The My Reviews page displays privileged approval requests you have permission to approve and reject.
Requester: The user who requested the privileged approval.
You can view the analytics of the privileged approval requests on the Requests page.
Console: The privileged console that the privileged approval request is set for.
Microtenant: The Microtenant associated with the privileged approval request.
Start Date: The set start time for access to the PRA Portal.
Requested Duration: The requested duration of time for access to the PRA Portal.
Approved Duration: The set duration of time for access to the PRA Portal. Access ends after this set time.
Pending: The privileged approval request is pending.
Approved: The privileged approval request is approved.
Expired: The privileged approval request is no longer available.
Rejected: The privileged approval request was rejected.

my-requests-and-reviews.conditions: The four statuses and the column list are quoted from the My Requests section; the page repeats the statuses under My Reviews, which is not separately quoted here. The admin Approval Requests page lists only Approved or Rejected (request-metadata).

my-approvals-filter.statement: The characters & and + cannot be used in the filter search field of the My Requests page or the My Reviews page.

quotes: The characters & and + cannot be used in the filter search field.
The characters & and + cannot be used in the filter search field.

portal-review.statement: After the admin has enabled privileged approvals in a portals policy, a reviewer can access the My Approvals page in the PRA Portal. When approving, Modify Time adjusts the time window of the request, an optional message can be included to the requester on approving or rejecting, and the request is then displayed as Approved or Rejected on the My Approvals page.

quotes: After the admin has enabled privileged approvals in a portals policy, you can access the My Approvals page in the PRA Portal.
Enable Modify Time if you want to adjust the time window of the request.
The approval request is displayed as Approved on the My Approvals page.
The approval request is displayed as Rejected on the My Approvals page.
(Optional) You can include a message to the requester.
(Optional) You can include a message to the requester.

segments-per-approval.summary: How many application segments a privileged approval can include: the Configuring Privileged Approvals page says there is no limit to the number that can be selected, and the Ranges and Limitations table gives 200 application segments per privileged approval.

quotes: There is no limit to the number you can select.

positions.says: There is no limit to the number of application segments that can be selected for an approval (said of the Application Segments field).

quotes: | Privileged Approvals | 20,000 privileged approvals 200 application segments per privileged approval

positions.says: A privileged approval can have 200 application segments (see zpa.pra.components:limits).

segments-per-approval.impact: An answer that a segment count caused a failed create, or that none can, should name both pages.

emergency-window-domains.summary: Whether the Add Emergency Access User window needs the email domain to be in the Emergency Authentication Domains field: the Configuring Privileged Approvals page lists that as a condition, and the Emergency Access page says, in its section for Private Access end users who have not migrated to Authentication Service, that users can be created from any non-primary, non-secondary domain when no domains are specified.

quotes: The specified email domain is added to the Emergency Authentication Domains field.

positions.says: One of the four conditions for the window to appear is that the email domain is added to the Emergency Authentication Domains field.

quotes: When no authentication domains are specified, users can be created from any authentication domain that is not an existing primary or secondary authentication domain.
evidence.after: For Private Access end users who have not migrated to Authentication Service

positions.says: In the Emergency Access page section for Private Access end users who have not migrated to Authentication Service, when no authentication domains are specified users can be created from any authentication domain that is not an existing primary or secondary one (see zpa.emergency-access.configuration:domains-semantics).

emergency-window-domains.impact: With the field empty it is not settled whether the window appears for a new domain. An answer about a missing window should not state either behaviour as fact.

working-hours-default.title: The default time zone and meaning of the working hours default
working-hours-default.detail: The Configuring Privileged Approvals page says the default is 9:00 start time and 17:00 end time for a 24-hour window, which is unclear, and the help does not state the default time zone. The SDK side is zpa.api.pra-wire:approval-times. A lab test would resolve it.

multi-approver.title: Requiring more than one approver
multi-approver.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Can we require 2-of-N approval? Not natively documented; approvals are 1-approver-approves model." The captured pages show one approve or reject action per request and no multi-approver setting, which is an absence and not a statement. A Zscaler statement or a configuration check would resolve it.

approval-optional.title: Which consoles require an approval
approval-optional.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Not all PRA consoles require approval - approval is configured per-policy." The access policy has an Allow with Privileged Approval checkbox (claim zpa.pra.access-policy:allow-with-privileged-approval), but the captured pages do not say that consoles without that setting skip approval. A lab test would resolve it.
